clue.text: Defence of old record, one held by a father

indicators.note: something held by another piece sits within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: PA is an informal word for a father
a log is a written record, as a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A historian defends an old document that a priest has been keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'father' is a letter of the answer, not a link word, and it stands outside the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence or justification of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Look sulky, having minor tangle with pests one's meant to soothe

indicators.note: a minor tangle means the letters are muddled a little

parts.note: to pout is to look sulky
lice are pests

explanation.surface: A sulking child, tangled up with lice, needs soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: POUT and LICE together give POUTLICE; 'minor tangle' swaps a couple of letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice is a soft moist dressing applied to soothe and draw out inflammation.

clue.text: Sorted out deal with play about church, given part in it

indicators.note: about means the letters go around the next piece
sorted out means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dispute over a church play is resolved, with someone given a part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' makes LADYAPEL; 'it' points back to church, so the definition is a part within a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lady Chapel is a chapel within a larger church dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Possibly varying art form to make easy profit

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Changing art forms could be a way to make easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' belongs to the definition; it is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy train is a source of easy money, a means of profiting with little effort.

clue.text: Given help, improved right away, but put in notice

indicators.note: put in means the other piece goes inside this one

parts.note: an ad is a notice in the paper

indicators.note: right away means the R for right is taken out

parts.note: better means improved

explanation.surface: A patient was helped and got better, but was given notice anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' leaves BETTE; 'but' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetted means assisted or encouraged, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Just clear

definitions.meaning: fine weather with no cloud or rain

explanation.definitionFit: A fair decision is just, and fair weather is clear and bright.

clue.text: Both finally failing in desire to take part in any TV show

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter
taking part in something means going inside it

parts.note: some can mean any, as in have you some
an itch is a desire

explanation.surface: Both of them fail at last in their wish to appear on any television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator serves both words: 'Both finally failing' strips the last letter from each before they combine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a situation comedy, a type of television show.

clue.text: Guarantee being circumspect, limiting tirade

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: being circumspect is being wary
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A cautious buyer seeks a guarantee to cut short a salesman's tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' means enclosing here; 'being circumspect' supplies an adjective, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee on goods.

clue.text: Swede perhaps used alloy, one with tin, mostly

parts.note: brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A Swedish metalworker uses an alloy plus a little tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from CAN, leaving CA. 'Swede' looks like a person, but it is the vegetable (the swede, or rutabaga).
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the cabbage genus, and the swede is one of its members, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Shoot had finally gone ahead for religious picture

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant

indicators.note: the final letter of the word had has moved up to the front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoot finally appeared before a religious painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally gone ahead' makes DHA. A statue or image of the Buddha is itself called a Buddha.
explanation.definitionFit: A Buddha is a statue or image of the Buddha, a familiar religious representation.

clue.text: Earliest of vehicles starting race aren't abused — one such?

definitions.text: Earliest of vehicles starting race aren't abused — one such?

indicators.note: the earliest letter of the following word is the only one used
abused means mistreated or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder; the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Old cars entered in a race have been knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' gives ETERANCAR; read as a whole, the clue describes an old car knocked about in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran car is, in Britain, one built before 1919, one of the earliest of motor vehicles.

clue.text: Scotch broth?

definitions.meaning: to scotch is to ruin or put an end to
a broth is one example of a prepared food course

explanation.surface: A bowl of Scottish soup.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish hopes is to scotch them, and a broth is a dish of food.

clue.text: Reserve place, in order to get in

parts.note: twelfth is a place in an ordered sequence
to man a boat or post is to get in and staff it

explanation.surface: A substitute is told to take a place in line to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the reserve player who fields when someone is injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team's twelfth man is its reserve, standing by to come on as substitute fielder.

clue.text: Say enough about fixing hunt's objective, at first

indicators.note: at first means this piece comes before the other
fixing means fastening RE inside the other word

parts.note: a fox is what a hunt pursues
RE means about or concerning
ample means enough

explanation.surface: Say enough about fixing the hunt's goal from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the definition in the sense 'for instance', not the verb it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: For example is used to introduce an instance, just as say does.

clue.text: Drank a lot of vintage wine, and went to bed

definitions.text: Drank a lot of vintage wine
definitions.meaning: sack is an old white wine, so to hit it is to drink a lot of it
a slang phrase for retiring for the night

explanation.surface: Someone drank heavily, then turned in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit the sack is slang for going to bed, and sack is also an old Spanish wine.

clue.text: Put on a new coat that doesn't need brushing

definitions.text: Put on a new coat that doesn't need brushing

parts.words: Put on a new coat that doesn't need brushing
parts.note: sounds like a person changing clothes, but it describes repainting a car with a spray gun rather than a brush

explanation.definitionFit: To respray a car is to give it a new coat of paint applied by spray, not brush.

clue.text: Mount extra support for expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: expedition can mean speed or haste, a rush
more means extra

explanation.surface: Climbers need extra support for a mountaineering expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey but means haste. MOUNT RUSHMORE is the US mountain carved with presidents' faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushmore is a mountain in South Dakota, so Mount names it.

clue.text: Please dull American, with healthy return on import

indicators.note: importing means taking something in, so these letters are brought inside the other word

parts.note: gray is the American spelling of grey, meaning dull

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: fit means healthy

explanation.surface: A dull American is cheered by a healthy return on imported goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' gives TIF. 'American' signals the US spelling with A, not the British grey.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone is to please or satisfy them.

clue.text: Voice of fine singer the group's drowned

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: something drowned is submerged inside, so this piece goes into the other

parts.note: an alto is a singer
a set is a group; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A fine singer's voice is drowned out by the band.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "group's" stands for 'is', so the group is what gets drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a high artificial singing voice used by men.

clue.text: Back cry to stop series only, halfway through

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so this piece goes inside
only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A tearful outburst stops a series halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: SER is the first half of SERIES; WEEP stops its gap. In football a sweeper is a defender playing behind the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a sweeper is a defensive player positioned behind the backs.

clue.text: It's given the impression saltwater fish grow larger

parts.note: the sea is saltwater
the ling is a long food fish of the cod family
to wax is to grow larger, as the moon waxes

explanation.surface: Saltwater fish seem to grow bigger in a fisherman's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the impression' means stamped with a seal, not misled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax is the substance into which a seal's design is pressed, so it is what receives the impression.

clue.text: Failed, being beaten away from home

indicators.note: being beaten means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team failed and was beaten playing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means away from home or at a distance, as in from far afield.

clue.text: Stop game

definitions.meaning: to stop or come to a standstill
game as an adjective means lame in the leg

explanation.definitionFit: A halt is a stop, and halt is also an old adjective meaning lame, like a game leg.

clue.text: Current type of jazz

definitions.meaning: the prevailing flow or trend, the main current of a river
a style of swing-era jazz that sits between traditional and modern

explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the main current or prevailing trend, and also a recognised style of jazz.

clue.text: TV channel

definitions.meaning: the television set, informally the box
a pipe or conduit for flow

explanation.definitionFit: The tube is slang for television, and a tube is also a channel or pipe.

clue.text: Flora left husband's underwear outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the underwear wraps round the other piece

parts.note: pants are underwear, here the husband's

explanation.surface: Flora walked out, leaving her husband's underpants out on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name, but it means plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora means the plant life of a region, so plants in general.

clue.text: On reflection, The Globe may be, in function

definitions.text: On reflection, The Globe may be, in function

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other

parts.note: a role is a function or job

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so this word is written backwards

parts.note: the globe is a ball, a sphere

explanation.surface: Reviewing The Globe newspaper, it may be in working order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' gives LLAB; read whole, the clue says a globe, being a ball, can be rolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollable means able to be rolled, which a ball-shaped globe certainly is.

clue.text: One may easily be undone by hazard; sailing at speed

parts.note: a reef is a hazard to shipping
a knot is a unit of speed at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor's knot may easily come apart, a hazard when sailing fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The reef knot is noted for being easy to untie.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a simple knot that can be undone easily by pulling one end, a sailor's favourite.
